decisions.executionNote: Holder is on the right and pens on the left. Begin right-hand side approach, gradually turning inward while preserving elbow-up continuity.
Advance the open right gripper toward the holder, completing most of the inward yaw. Observe clearance before closing.
Bring right fingers forward and inward to the holder's side, with small downward increments; keep jaws open for alignment.
Correct forward alignment of the right jaws with the holder; maintain height and orientation before grasping.
Holder shifted under the forward finger. Withdraw sideways before realigning, avoiding further pushing.
Align the open right jaws farther forward with the shifted holder, then approach laterally in small increments.
Holder is being contacted off-center. Back away fully in the lateral direction before further forward alignment; allow it to settle upright.
The holder has tipped. Retract and raise the right wrist, turning toward a top-down recovery grasp rather than pushing it farther.
Previous recovery motion was rejected with zero movement. Use much smaller retreat increments and ease away from the wrist yaw limit before changing pitch.
Continue a small, clear retreat and unwind yaw to gain wrist motion margin, then start a gentle downward pitch for holder recovery.
Approach above the fallen holder with open jaws, gradually pitching downward while keeping the right arm on its side.
Finish orienting downward above the holder and shift toward its center. Keep the gripper open until its sides are bracketed.
Pitch continuation hit an IK boundary. Keep the accepted orientation and lower toward the holder with small translation increments to regain configuration margin.
Ease the downward pitch toward a shallower side grasp, relieving the folded reach limit without advancing the rejected translation.
Close around the fallen holder at the current aligned side position, then test retention with a short lift and retreat.
The holder stayed on the table and the fingers closed together above it. Reopen and lower to bracket the sidewalls before retrying.
Lower another small amount around the holder's width, then close at rest. Check actual finger separation and retention before transporting.
Test the holder grasp by lifting and drawing it back from the far edge; maintain closed jaws throughout.
Holder appears retained. Lift clear and bring it back into the right workspace while beginning to turn its opening upward.
Continue rolling the securely held holder toward upright, keeping it in the right workspace and at a steady raised height.
Finish righting the holder and lower it to a practical insertion height; verify the opening orientation from the next view.
Replan the holder motion from the observed pose with smaller rotations and a backward translation for margin. Begin raising the left hand toward the pens.
Raise the retained holder without further wrist rotation to gain articulation margin. Move the left open gripper above the nearest purple pen.
The previous call executed zero steps. Use a small orientation bridge to the last accepted target, then gently raise the holder for wrist clearance.
Center the left downward-facing gripper over the near purple pen. Use the gained elevation to continue righting the holder without forcing the wrist stop.
Align the left jaws with the purple marker and descend slowly. Shift the retained holder forward to gain room for a lower upright holding pose.
Close the left gripper on the purple marker and test with a short lift. Lower the holder while easing its pitch away from the wrist limit.
Lift and turn the retained purple marker toward vertical. Continue lowering the holder cautiously while maintaining the grasp and wrist clearance.
The marker did not follow the left gripper; reopen and return for a lower grasp. Roll the holder toward the camera to bring its opening upward.
Raise the right wrist without rotation to leave its pitch stop. Finish the left downward approach at a lower pen-grasp height with jaws open.
Zero steps executed on the last attempt. Bridge slightly toward the accepted orientation first, then lift the holder without further rotation; use smaller left approach increments.
Center the near marker between the left jaws and close at the lower height. Continue a slow holder roll while raising enough to preserve wrist margin.
Lift the now-bracketed marker to check retention. Make a small final holder tilt correction while moving forward to improve lowering clearance.
Both objects appear retained. Turn the marker upright while lifting; bring the holder forward and slightly down, easing wrist pitch for clearance.
Finish making the marker vertical. With gained forward reach margin, lower the holder and roll its remaining away-from-camera tilt toward upright.
The holder opening is visible from the left wrist. Bring it back from the forward joint boundary while raising the upright marker toward the opening, keeping both grips closed.
No movement on the rejected call. Reduce the right retreat to 2 mm increments to preserve joint continuity; continue a gradual marker lift.
The upright holder's recovery grasp prevents safe lowering at the wrist limit. Release it upright to settle on the clear table, then regrasp its side; keep the marker retained away from it.
Holder settled on its side. Reorient the right hand for a top-down recovery grasp so the subsequent righting motion ends in a normal side-holding pose. Move the retained marker clear.
Use smaller orientation and translation increments through the wrist transition. Keep the marker out of the recovery path.
Position the right wrist over the fallen holder and pitch downward for a grasp that can rotate into a normal upright side hold.
The last action was rejected before movement. Halve the wrist transition and approach increments to preserve joint continuity.
Continue the downward-facing recovery approach, moving the wrist toward the holder center as the fingertip offset rotates.
Align over the fallen holder's center, finishing a near-vertical approach with the jaws spanning its width. Keep the held marker stationary.
Keep the accepted recovery orientation and translate slowly down and forward to center the holder between the open jaws.
Back off the steep recovery pitch and translate toward the robot to leave the IK boundary. Keep the marker stationary and gripped.
The previous retreat executed zero steps. Quarter the increments to exit the near-singular configuration continuously.
Move the open right grasp forward onto the holder, compensating the fingertip offset while reducing pitch slightly to maintain joint margin.
The steep forward reach hit an IK boundary. Shallow the approach and yaw toward the holder to regain continuity and center the open fingertips.
No motion executed. Quarter the adjustment to leave the near-singular configuration without an IK joint jump.
Back out of the tight recovery reach and reverse the last orientation adjustment to restore elbow configuration margin before approaching again.
Use a shallower recovery angle, moving the wrist outward and forward while maintaining approximately the same fingertip height to center over the holder.
Clear the holder vertically before any further forward correction. Ease the steep wrist angle to leave the constrained recovery configuration.
With the fingers clear above the holder, shift forward to its center before descending. Keep the left marker retained and stationary.
The forward shift was rejected with zero movement. Reduce the shift and rotation substantially to maintain continuity near the current joint boundary.
Replan from the executed prefix: keep the accepted orientation and lower in small increments, moving slightly outward for arm clearance.
The lowering prefix reached an IK discontinuity. Retreat toward the right arm's base at fixed orientation to restore reach margin before descending.
Only one retreat step executed. Change the wrist yaw gently away from the constrained inward orientation instead of continuing the rejected translation.
The yaw adjustment was rejected without motion. Try a short diagonal retreat at fixed orientation to move away from the constrained reach, subject to the joint guard.
The diagonal retreat was rejected. Use a one-millimeter reverse adjustment and settle, avoiding further motion until the IK branch is stable.
The held pose settled but the folded reach remains constrained. Test the opposite small yaw direction at fixed position to regain continuous motion.
Use sub-millimeter position changes at fixed orientation to back out of the extension boundary without the large IK change seen on earlier retreats.
The sub-millimeter retreat restored continuity. Lower with a shallower side approach, maintaining a backward margin rather than pushing farther into full extension.
Continue lowering with smaller increments after the wrist tracking interruption; keep the open jaws aligned around the holder's projected sides.
Shift the right jaws a small distance forward at fixed height to center the holder before the final descent and closure.
Lower the right jaws to the holder's sidewalls, then close at rest. Confirm retention before attempting another righting motion.
The jaws closed in front of the holder, and lowering met the table. Reopen and correct the forward alignment without pressing down.
The holder is now visually between the right fingers. Close at rest and test with a small lift and backward motion, leaving the reach boundary.
The right jaws closed empty above the holder. Reopen and lower at fixed horizontal alignment to reach its sidewalls without pushing it farther away.
Make a small forward centering correction at the achieved lower height, then close without descending into the table.
The holder appears too close to the right palm rather than between the fingertip pads. Reopen and move outward to correct grasp depth at the same height.
The far-side approach is constrained by reach. Withdraw backward and upward, turning toward a front approach that reaches the holder without extending farther forward.
The previous retreat executed zero steps. Reduce initial retreat and rotation increments to preserve continuity at the current wrist configuration.
With reach margin restored, swing the open right hand to approach the holder from the near side, staying clear above the table.
Lower the open right hand toward the holder from the newly accessible near-side direction, with a small wrist-view centering correction.
Advance along the near-side approach with open jaws, lowering only slightly to bring the holder's sidewalls between the pads.
Make a small lateral centering adjustment, close around the near-side holder wall, and test with a short vertical lift without further table contact.
Test whether the narrow edge grasp retained the holder by lifting and drawing it back into the right workspace, without changing orientation.
The holder remained on the table. Correct the substantial sideways offset indicated by the wrist view, returning open jaws toward the holder center rather than the previous empty grasp.
The wrist view shows the prior lateral correction was in the wrong direction. Reverse it to bring the holder back between the open jaws, with slight table clearance.
Finish the lateral centering correction at the current safe height and close on the holder without further downward pressure.
Closed fingers are still above the holder rather than retaining it. Reopen and back along the approach to align the object with the distal pads instead of the palm.
The holder is centered at the distal opening after retreating. Close here and check a short vertical lift for actual retention.
The lift confirmed an empty grasp. Advance the open near-side approach farther toward the holder, using the head view to resolve the remaining depth gap.
The jaws are spanning the holder's length rather than its width. Clear the table and roll the open gripper to clamp across the shorter dimension.
Lower the reoriented jaws toward the holder's shorter cross-section, with small centering increments and no closure until aligned.
Close the vertically oriented jaws at the reached contact height, then lift and retreat slightly to test whether the holder follows.
The holder is left and below the empty grasp. Restore horizontal jaw closure while correcting that lateral and height offset, keeping the right wrist on its side.
Correct the rightward wrist-view offset and descend toward the holder's actual sidewall height. Keep the jaws open and preserve clearance above the tabletop.
The horizontal jaws span the holder's long axis. Lift clear and roll the jaws to clamp its shorter vertical cross-section, then approach at the corrected height.
Close the vertical jaws gradually while lowering slightly, avoiding a fully open lower finger striking the table. Check for holder retention before lifting.
The right fingers closed empty with a small contact residual. Withdraw the palm from the holder, then lower the partially open vertical jaws toward its cross-section.
Vertical side closure is blocked by the table. Lift clear and change to an angled top grasp with the jaws across the holder's short width.
Complete the angled top-grasp orientation while compensating the fingertip offset, keeping the holder centered and the right wrist on its side.
